entries.name: Git Hygiene

payload.content:
---
name: git-hygiene
description: Clean commits, branch names, and PR descriptions.
---

# Git Hygiene Skill

1. **Atomic commits** — one logical change per commit.
2. **Message format** — `<area>: <imperative summary>` under 72 chars, body explains *why*.
3. **Branches** — `feat/`, `fix/`, `chore/` prefixes, short kebab-case names.
4. **PRs** — link the issue, list test evidence, keep diffs reviewable (<400 lines).
5. **Never** force-push shared branches or commit secrets.

entries.name: Web Scraping
entries.creator: mvp-labs
entries.description: Respectful, robust web scraping patterns.

payload.content:
---
name: web-scraping
description: Respectful, robust web scraping patterns.
---

# Web Scraping Skill

1. **Respect the site** — check robots.txt and ToS first; identify with a
   real User-Agent; rate-limit (1 req/s default); cache aggressively.
2. **Prefer APIs** — look for a JSON API, RSS feed, or sitemap before
   parsing HTML.
3. **Robust selectors** — prefer semantic attributes (data-*, aria-label)
   over fragile CSS paths; handle pagination and retries with backoff.
4. **Anti-bot reality** — rotate UA/IP only where legal; never bypass
   CAPTCHAs or login walls without permission.
5. **Store raw** — save raw responses before parsing so re-parses are free.

entries.name: PDF Processing
entries.creator: mvp-labs
entries.description: Extract text and tables from PDFs reliably.

payload.content:
---
name: pdf-processing
description: Extract text and tables from PDFs reliably.
---

# PDF Processing Skill

1. **Text first** — try text extraction (pdfminer/pypdf); fall back to OCR
   (tesseract) only for scanned pages.
2. **Tables** — use camelot/tabula for ruled tables; verify column alignment
   on the first page before batch runs.
3. **Structure** — preserve headings and page numbers; emit markdown with
   `#` hierarchy matching the document.
4. **Large docs** — process page ranges in parallel; stream output, never
   hold the whole book in memory twice.
5. **Quality check** — spot-check 5 random pages against the source PDF.

entries.name: CSV Cleaning
entries.creator: mvp-labs
entries.description: Tidy messy CSVs: encodings, delimiters, types, dedupe.

payload.content:
---
name: csv-cleaning
description: Tidy messy CSVs: encodings, delimiters, types, dedupe.
---

# CSV Cleaning Skill

1. **Detect** — sniff encoding (utf-8-sig vs latin-1) and delimiter before
   parsing; never assume commas.
2. **Types** — coerce dates/numbers explicitly; quarantine unparseable
   values into an `_errors` column instead of dropping rows silently.
3. **Dedupe** — define the natural key first; keep the newest complete row.
4. **Normalize** — trim whitespace, unify case for keys, standardize
   null representations (NA, n/a, -, empty).
5. **Report** — emit a cleaning log: rows in/out, columns changed, error
   counts. Reproducible script over manual edits, always.

entries.name: API Integration
entries.creator: mvp-labs
entries.description: Consume REST APIs: auth, pagination, retries, rate limits.

payload.content:
---
name: api-integration
description: Consume REST APIs: auth, pagination, retries, rate limits.
---

# API Integration Skill

1. **Read the docs** — auth scheme, pagination style, rate limits, and
   error codes before writing a line.
2. **Auth hygiene** — tokens from env vars, never hardcoded; refresh
   proactively before expiry.
3. **Pagination** — follow cursor/next links, not page arithmetic; dedupe
   by resource id.
4. **Resilience** — exponential backoff on 429/5xx; circuit-break after
   repeated failures; idempotency keys on writes.
5. **Respect** — cache GETs, batch where supported, stay under limits.

entries.name: Data Visualization
entries.creator: mvp-labs
entries.description: Choosing the right chart and keeping it honest.

payload.content:
---
name: data-viz
description: Choosing the right chart and keeping it honest.
---

# Data Visualization Skill

1. **Chart selection** — trends → line; comparisons → bar; distribution →
   histogram/box; part-of-whole → bar (pie only for 2–3 slices);
   relationship → scatter.
2. **Honest axes** — bars start at zero; label axes and units; never
   truncate an axis to exaggerate.
3. **One message per chart** — title states the takeaway, not the topic.
4. **Reduce ink** — remove gridlines, 3D, and decoration that carry no data.
5. **Color** — one highlight color for the story, gray for the rest;
   colorblind-safe palettes.

entries.name: Code Review
entries.creator: mvp-labs
entries.description: Checklist for reviews that catch real bugs.

payload.content:
---
name: code-review
description: Checklist for reviews that catch real bugs.
---

# Code Review Skill

1. **Correctness first** — edge cases, off-by-ones, null handling, error
   paths. Ask: "what breaks this?"
2. **Security** — injection, auth checks, secrets, unvalidated input.
3. **Performance** — N+1 queries, accidental O(n²), unbounded growth.
4. **Readability** — names, function size, comments where intent is
   non-obvious. Suggest, don't dictate.
5. **Scope** — review the diff, not the author's career. Approve fast when
   it's right; block only on real issues.

entries.name: Blog Posts
entries.creator: mvp-labs
entries.description: Structure and voice for technical blog posts.

payload.content:
---
name: blog-posts
description: Structure and voice for technical blog posts.
---

# Blog Posts Skill

1. **Hook** — first paragraph states the problem and the payoff.
2. **Structure** — problem → approach → implementation → results →
   takeaways. Subheads every 300 words.
3. **Code** — minimal complete examples; show output; link the repo.
4. **Voice** — concrete over clever; "we tried X" beats "one might X".
5. **Close** — one actionable takeaway and a question for readers.

entries.name: Cron Scheduling
entries.creator: mvp-labs
entries.description: Cron expressions and scheduling gotchas.

payload.content:
---
name: cron-scheduling
description: Cron expressions and scheduling gotchas.
---

# Cron Scheduling Skill

1. **Format** — `min hour dom month dow`; `*/15 * * * *` = every 15 min.
2. **Timezone** — cron runs in server time; document which TZ the schedule
   assumes. Prefer UTC for servers.
3. **Overlap** — jobs longer than the interval need locking (flock) or
   idempotency keys.
4. **Silent failures** — redirect output to logs; alert on non-zero exit;
   test with a 1-minute schedule first.
5. **DST** — twice-yearly surprises; avoid 01:00–03:00 local for critical
   jobs.

entries.name: Competitive Analysis
entries.creator: mvp-labs
entries.description: Structured competitor teardowns.

payload.content:
---
name: competitive-analysis
description: Structured competitor teardowns.
---

# Competitive Analysis Skill

1. **Frame** — the job-to-be-done, not the feature list. Who is it for?
2. **Evidence** — pricing pages, docs, reviews, changelogs. Date every
   claim; screenshots beat memory.
3. **Matrix** — capabilities × competitors, one row per job-to-be-done.
4. **Moat check** — what would it cost them to copy your edge?
5. **So what** — end with 3 implications for your roadmap, not a dump.

entries.name: Copywriting
entries.creator: mvp-labs
entries.description: Headlines and CTAs that convert.

payload.content:
---
name: copywriting
description: Headlines and CTAs that convert.
---

# Copywriting Skill

1. **Headlines** — specific > clever. Numbers, timeframes, and outcomes.
   Write 10, keep 3.
2. **Body** — one idea per paragraph; benefits before features; proof
   (numbers, names) before claims.
3. **CTA** — one per piece; verb + outcome ("Start saving today").
4. **Voice** — match the reader's words, not your team's jargon.
5. **Edit** — cut 20% on the second pass; read it aloud.

entries.name: SQL Helper
entries.creator: mvp-labs
entries.description: Portable SQL patterns and dialect notes.

payload.content:
---
name: sql-helper
description: Portable SQL patterns and dialect notes.
---

# SQL Helper Skill

1. **Portability** — prefer standard SQL; isolate dialect quirks (LIMIT vs
   TOP vs FETCH) in one place.
2. **Readability** — CTEs over nested subqueries; explicit JOINs; alias
   consistently.
3. **Correctness** — mind NULL semantics, duplicates from JOIN fan-out, and
   timezone handling in timestamps.
4. **Performance** — filter early, select only needed columns, check the
   plan (EXPLAIN) before optimizing blindly.
5. **Safety** — parameterized queries always; never string-concatenate user
   input into SQL.
